assertions.statement: Allen County peaked in 1980, not 1970. It has fallen at every count since, from 112,241 to 100,866.

citations.span: **The county's peak is 1980, not 1970, and the corpus has been saying 1970 since genesis.**

citations.node_label: The depopulation of Lima and Allen County
citations.span: Between 1970 and 1980 the county *grew*, from 111,144 to **112,241** — its highest count ever — before falling to 109,755 in 1990 and 108,464 in 2000

citations.node_label: The depopulation of Lima and Allen County

caveats: It does not establish that either mechanism reaches back before 2020.

It does not establish that the decline has ended: fifteen people on 100,851 is far inside what a modelled estimate can resolve, one year is not a direction, and the same programme revises its own earlier years with every vintage.
This corpus does not establish that Lima is emptying because it is aging.
It does not establish that the county's population decline was caused by its manufacturing decline.

assertions.statement: The loss is concentrated in Lima: between 2000 and 2010 the city fell 3.8 per cent while the rest of the county fell 1.5 per cent.

citations.node_label: The depopulation of Lima and Allen County
citations.span: between 2000 and 2010 Lima fell 3.8% while the balance of Allen County — everything outside every incorporated place — fell 1.5%, from 50,809 to 50,048

caveats: It does not establish that either mechanism reaches back before 2020.

It does not establish that the decline has ended: fifteen people on 100,851 is far inside what a modelled estimate can resolve, one year is not a direction, and the same programme revises its own earlier years with every vintage.
This corpus does not establish that Lima is emptying because it is aging.
It does not establish that the county's population decline was caused by its manufacturing decline.

assertions.statement: The oil made the city: Lima went from 7,567 people in 1880 to 41,326 in 1920, and on to its peak of 53,734 in 1970.

citations.span: **Lima peaked at the 1970 census.**

assertions.statement: Allen County has a population count at every decennial census from 1830 to 2020: 578 at the first and 102,217 at the last, with the peak in 1980.
The city peaked in 1970, the county in 1980, and the county outside the city in 2000.

citations.span: **So the county has three peaks and they are thirty years apart.** Lima peaked in 1970, the county as a whole in 1980, and the county outside Lima in 2000.

assertions.statement: Every one of the county's twelve townships is larger now than it was in 1930 — and larger than in 1890 too, which is the harder test, because 1930 was near the bottom.

citations.span: **Every one of the twelve is larger now than it was in 1930, and the comparison is sound.**
The whole balance is two and a half times its 1930 size while the county is below its 1980 peak and the city has lost a third of itself.
**But 1930 was near the bottom, and the second column is why that matters.**

assertions.statement: Lima had 3,607 manufacturing wage earners in 1909, up from 1,980 in 1899 — and these are the only measurements of work this corpus holds, all of them sixty years before the decline it describes.

citations.span: **Lima had 85 manufacturing establishments in 1909 employing 3,607 wage earners on average, against 2,733 in 1904 and 1,980 in 1899.**
**The city's workforce grew 82 per cent in a decade and its output grew 25.**

assertions.statement: Twenty-five years after the oil strike, Allen County had more farms than before it — 2,939 against 2,858 — on 92.5 per cent of its land area.

citations.node_label: Allen County farms and farm property, 1900–1910
citations.span: **The county had 2,939 farms in 1910 and 2,858 in 1900, on 240,472 acres against 245,283.**

citations.node_label: Allen County farms and farm property, 1900–1910
citations.span: **Nine-tenths of Allen County was farmland in 1910 — 240,472 acres of 259,840, or 92.5 per cent.**

assertions.statement: Nine separately elected offices govern Allen County and eleven people hold them, because the board of commissioners seats three.

citations.span: **Nine separately elected offices govern Allen County, and eleven people hold them, because the board of commissioners seats three.**

assertions.statement: Allen County's biggest building decade was the 1970s — 8,298 homes — and 6,333 of them went up outside Lima, in the decade the city reached its own peak.

citations.node_label: When Allen County's housing was built, 2023
citations.span: **The county's biggest building decade was the 1970s**, 8,298 units ± 585 against 6,529 ± 563 for the 1950s.

citations.node_label: When Allen County's housing was built, 2023
citations.span: **Six thousand three hundred and thirty-three of those 8,298 were built outside Lima.** The city took 1,965 of the decade in which it reached its own peak of 53,734 and held 48.4 per cent of the county.

caveats: Marion at 37.0 per cent and Richland at 38.0 read higher than Lima and this does not establish that they are older: 1,069 ± 235 of 2,886 ± 242 and 930 ± 195 of 2,449 ± 168 leave all three indistinguishable.
This does not establish why the housing was built where it was.

assertions.statement: Allen County is 68.3 per cent owner-occupied, which is an ordinary American figure made of Lima at 46.4 per cent and twelve townships between 72.0 and 91.0.

citations.node_label: Allen County housing units, occupancy, tenure and value, 2023
citations.span: Allen County is 68.3 per cent owner-occupied against 65.0 nationally — an unremarkable figure made of Lima at 46.4 per cent and twelve townships between 72.0 and 91.0, the city being the only subdivision below 70.

caveats: Perry Township's 17.0 per cent is the highest figure in the vacancy column, and this does not establish that it is the county's emptiest place: 290 vacant units ± 130 puts the rate between 9.4 and 24.7 per cent, straddling Lima's 11.5.

assertions.statement: Across 2018–2024, mortgages to buy a house in Lima's census tracts were denied at 13.3 per cent against 10.8 elsewhere in the county. Loans against a house already owned there were denied at 37.7 per cent against 21.5.

citations.span: Over 2018–2024 the purchase denial rate in Lima's tracts is 13.3 per cent against 10.8 elsewhere — 363 denials of 2,737 against 645 of 5,996 — and Lima's rate is the higher one in six of the seven years.
On everything but purchase, Lima's rate is 37.7 per cent against 21.5 — 1,104 denials of 2,926 against 2,000 of 9,289.

caveats: This does not establish why either gap is there.

assertions.statement: Across 2018–2024, mortgage applications from Black applicants in Allen County were denied at 32.4 per cent and from white applicants at 17.8, and the gap appears in all seven years.

citations.node_label: Allen County mortgage denial rates by applicant race, 2018-2024
citations.span: **It is a pattern and not a year.** Pooled over the seven, 32.4 per cent of applications from Black applicants were denied against 17.8 per cent from white applicants, and the yearly gap runs between 5.9 and 17.0 percentage points without once reversing.

caveats: This does not establish that any applicant was treated differently.

assertions.statement: Sorted into cells of loan purpose, income, debt-to-income and loan-to-value, 955 applications from Black applicants in Allen County drew 223 denials where 132.5 were expected at the white rate in the same cells.

citations.node_label: Allen County mortgage denial rates by applicant race, 2018-2024
citations.span: Those 955 drew **223 denials against 132.5 expected at the white rate in the same cells**, a ratio of 1.68 and 9.3 standard deviations from the null.

caveats: This does not establish that any applicant was treated differently.

assertions.statement: Mortgage applications from Black applicants in Allen County were denied at 37.9 per cent and from white applicants at 22.6, and the gap holds inside every income band this corpus can cut.

citations.node_label: Allen County mortgage applications and denials, 2023
citations.span: **Applications from Black applicants were denied at 37.9 per cent and from white applicants at 22.6** — 66 of 174 against 458 of 2,023 — and the gap holds inside every income band the corpus cut. Under $50,000: 45.3 against 33.4. From $50,000 to $99,000: 38.0 against 20.5. At $100,000 and over: 25.6 against 15.8.
